## Overview

This lab is **Phase 2** of the [Project Toolkit](../../project/project-toolkit.qmd). You will finalise stimulus materials, complete the Researcher Procedure, add the Recruitment Script and Data Recording Sheet, **practice running the study** on each other, and complete the Research Study Order Form.

**Week 19 lab is data collection.** You must finish all toolkit documents in **Weeks 17 and 18** so you are ready to collect data in Week 19.

---

## Why Phase 2 Matters

- **Stimulus materials** and **Data Recording Sheet** ensure you have consistent, scorable data.
- A **complete Researcher Procedure** ensures every session is run the same way.
- A **practice run** reveals unclear instructions, timing problems, and scoring issues *before* real participants arrive.
- The **Research Study Order Form** ensures everything is printed and available on data collection day.

---

## Document 4: Recruitment Script

**What it is:** A short script your group uses to approach potential participants and invite them to take part.

**Who sees it:** Researchers only — you read or paraphrase it when recruiting.

**Tips:** Keep it brief and friendly (3–4 sentences). Mention: who you are, what the study involves (briefly), how long it takes, where to go, and any incentive (e.g. snacks). Print several copies so multiple group members can recruit at once. Use the toolkit template.

---

## Document 5: Data Recording Sheet

**What it is:** A table where you record each participant's data: participant number, condition (if between-subjects), DV score, and any optional demographics.

**Who sees it:** Researchers only — you fill it in after scoring each participant.

**Tips:** Include a **scoring guide** so all group members score the DV consistently. The template has tables for both between- and within-subjects designs — delete the one you don't need. This is your raw data, so accuracy and consistency matter. Finalise by end of Week 18.

---

## Document 6: Stimulus Materials

**What it is:** The actual materials participants interact with — word lists, images, passages, rating sheets, questionnaires, etc.

**Who sees it:** Participants (during the study) and researchers.

**Tips:** Match materials across conditions (e.g. word frequency, difficulty, length). See the [Project Options](../../project/group-project-options.qmd) and the worked example in the toolkit for your project type. Test your materials on each other before data collection day. Finalise by the end of Week 18.

---

## Document 8: Researcher Procedure (Complete)

**What it is:** The full step-by-step guide for the researcher. You **started** this in Phase 1; in Phase 2 you **complete** it.

**Add or finalise:**

- **Data recording**: When and how you fill in the Data Recording Sheet (e.g. after each participant; where to write condition and score).
- **Scoring**: How you score the DV; reference to the scoring guide on the Data Recording Sheet.
- **Full script**: Every phrase the participant hears (in quotes or italics), including greeting, instructions, and debrief.
- **Timing**: Duration for each phase (study period, distractor, recall, etc.).
- **Materials checklist**: Everything to prepare before each testing session.

Any group member should be able to run the study from this document alone. Use the between- or within-subjects example procedure in the toolkit as a reference.

---

## Practice Run

Running the study on each other **before** data collection day helps you:

- Check that **timing** is realistic (not too long or too short).
- Find **unclear instructions** or missing steps.
- Agree on **scoring** (everyone uses the scoring guide the same way).
- Update the **Researcher Procedure** and **Participant Instructions** with any fixes.

**How:** One person runs as researcher, others as participants. Use a timer and the Data Recording Sheet. Debrief: what was confusing? Then swap if time, and update the documents.

---

## Document 9: Research Study Order Form

**What it is:** A form listing everything your group needs printed or provided for data collection day. You submit it to Gordon so resources can be prepared in advance.

**When:** Submit by **end of Week 18** at latest (Week 19 lab is data collection).

**Tips:** List every document and how many copies (err on the side of more). Include any special requirements (e.g. colour printing, specific paper size). Don't forget consumables: pens, blank paper for recall, snacks. Use the toolkit template.

---

## Preparation for the Lab

- Bring your **Phase 1 drafts** (Information Sheet, Consent, Debrief, Participant Instructions, Researcher Procedure).
- Re-read the Project Toolkit checklist for documents 4, 5, 6, 8, 9.
- Download the **templates** for Recruitment Script, Data Recording Sheet, Stimulus Materials (if using template), and Research Study Order Form.
- Have your **design** (between/within) and **DV** (and scoring rule) clear so you can complete the Data Recording Sheet and procedure.
